article_title: Worth the Effort: the Start and Stick to Desirable Difficulties (S2D2) Framework
citation: Anique B. H. de Bruin, Felicitas Biwer, Luotong Hui, Erdem Onan, Louise David, Wisnu Wiradhany. (2023). Worth the Effort: the Start and Stick to Desirable Difficulties (S2D2) Framework. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09766-w
title: S2D2 framework: supporting self-regulation of effort when engaging in desirable difficulties
description: The S2D2 framework describes how learners can be supported to self-regulate effort when engaging in desirable difficulties, building on the Effort Monitoring and Regulation model. It centers on the interrelations between perceived effort, perceived learning, and use of desirable difficulties, and organizes support into accepting, reducing, or silencing perceived effort. As the authors state, "Here, we present a framework that describes how to support self-regulation of effort when engaging in desirable difficulties: the \"Start and Stick to Desirable Difficulties (S2D2)\" framework." The framework targets self-study contexts with (older) adolescents and adult learners.
requirements: Support depends on addressing perceived effort, perceived learning, and actual learning effects simultaneously
constraints: The framework focuses on learners' self-regulated use of desirable difficulties in the self-study context, not on how teachers directly incorporate desirable difficulties in teaching
target_learners: older adolescents and adult learners in self-study contexts
target_learning_goals: self-regulated use of effective, desirably difficult learning strategies such as retrieval practice and interleaving
examples: The framework organizes interventions at strategy, task, and learner levels into accept, reduce, or silence approaches (Table 1)
